## What changed

**Nothing was changed on this task, because the optimizer never saw it.** The N=30 pilot's `val` split contained 2 tasks (`traces_parsec-aap2-0047` and `-0048`); this is one of the other 28. It has exactly one measurement in the whole experiment: a single trial in the reference sweep.

## What worked

Everything the contract asks for. The seed skill reproduced the full 4-call trajectory (`trajectory: 1.000`) **and** hit all 5 `answer_contains` assertions, for a reward of exactly **1.000** — the only task in v1 to do so.

## What didn't

Nothing failed. But note what "solved" means here: this is one of only 5 v1 tasks whose entire demanded sequence was callable against the simulators that were up, and trajectory matched on 5/5 of those. The score is real; it is also drawn from the only part of the set where a trajectory match was possible at all.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**This is a ceiling artifact, not a result.** A task already at 1.000 carries no optimizer signal — there is nothing for a candidate to improve and every direction is down. It inflates any pass-rate headline computed over all 30 tasks while contributing zero information about whether cap-evolve works. It is also a single trial: at n=1, 1.000 is not a claim that the skill solves this task reliably, only that it did once.
